final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced merger with UBS as the only viable path, requiring execution by Sunday evening with a government loss guarantee (CHF 6-10bn), SNB liquidity backstop (CHF 100-200bn), AT1 write-down, and purchase price of CHF 0.50-1.00/share.
minority_objections: SNB concerned about CHF 100-200bn balance sheet exposure and inflation risk from massive liquidity injection
UBS shareholders face short-term value destruction from CHF 10-15bn integration costs and execution risk
key_conflicts: FINMA vs AT1 bondholders: must write down AT1 to make deal viable while facing legal/reputational blowback for violating capital hierarchy
Federal Council vs taxpayers: committing CHF 6-10bn guarantee faces voter fury
UBS leverage vs government desperation: UBS can extort maximum concessions because no Plan B exists
AT1 bondholders vs deal structure: writing down CHF 16bn AT1 while equity gets UBS offer inverts normal hierarchy
key_concessions: Federal Council to UBS: CHF 6-10bn loss guarantee, CHF 100bn+ SNB liquidity, 12-24 month capital ratio forbearance, antitrust waiver
FINMA to UBS: regulatory forbearance, fast-track approvals, acceptance of 60%+ Swiss market share
UBS to Federal Council: accepts reputational risk and integration chaos in exchange for massive subsidies
AT1 bondholders: receive 0-30% recovery, lose CHF 11-16bn, accept 3-5 year litigation
Credit Suisse: accepts sale at CHF 0.50-1.00/share (80-90% loss vs Friday close of CHF 1.86)
red_lines: UBS demands government absorbs first CHF 6-10bn of losses as condition of deal
UBS demands AT1 write-down (CHF 16bn) as condition to reduce liabilities before acquisition
Federal Council position: UBS cooperation is non-negotiable, license depends on participation
SNB demands first-priority claim on CS assets and government indemnity if losses exceed CHF 10bn
Timeline constraint: all decisions must be finalized by Sunday 21:00 before Asian markets open
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Operational integration chaos: acknowledged that Day 1 IT/operations failures are likely but dismissed as manageable with 2-4 weeks client service disruption
Wealth client flight: noted 10-20% will leave Swiss system entirely over 6 months but not treated as deal-breaker
International coordination failure with ECB/Fed/BoE treated as secondary risk despite CS being major global ISDA participant
Political revolt probability estimated at 50-60% but accepted as inevitable cost rather than constraint on deal structure
downstream_risk_variables: UBS refusal probability (30-40%) - if UBS refuses, no Plan B exists and CS collapses Monday
Weekend deposit run acceleration (60-70% probability of CHF 50-100bn outflow)
AT1 litigation success: 3-5 year legal battle with possible CHF 3-5bn settlement in 2026-2028
Systemic AT1 market freeze: European banks face CHF 50-100bn higher funding costs globally
CS operational capability: even with liquidity, may be unable to open branches/systems if run continues
Parliamentary constitutional challenges to Federal Council emergency powers on Monday morning
uncertainty_notes: Critical uncertainties remaining: (1) whether UBS will accept deal on any terms or demand impossible conditions, (2) exact AT1 write-down percentage (full vs partial) and resulting litigation exposure, (3) whether weekend deposit run can be contained with SNB liquidity alone or requires withdrawal restrictions/bank holiday, (4) political sustainability of deal structure given 50-60% probability of public revolt, (5) operational feasibility of merging two global banks in 62 hours

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Explicit statement that 'standalone recapitalization is not viable within 62 hours' and 'no investor will commit material capital to a franchise bleeding deposits' - drove rejection of liquidity-only path
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition is the 'Primary Recommendation' and 'ONLY Swiss institution with balance sheet and capacity to absorb CS rapidly enough' - entire decision structure built around this path
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 6-10bn loss guarantee and CHF 100-200bn SNB liquidity are mandatory components of the deal structure - UBS demands government absorbs first losses as red line condition
marker_evidence.client_flight: Deposit run listed as 'DECISIVE RISK R2' with 60-70% probability of CHF 50-100bn weekend outflow driving operational inability to open Monday - shapes liquidity facility size and timing urgency
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down is Decision D5 (must-decide by Sunday) and UBS red-line demand to reduce CHF 16bn liabilities - drives specific deal structure and loss allocation
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Listed as 'DECISIVE RISK R3' and 'key conflict' - AT1 write-down while equity gets UBS offer 'inverts normal hierarchy' and drives litigation exposure acceptance and potential partial write-down compromise
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 litigation acknowledged with 40-50% probability and CHF 3-5bn settlement exposure, but decision is to 'impose write-down via FINMA emergency order and litigate later' - recognized but accepted rather than constraining
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 62-hour timeline to Monday market open is the binding constraint - all decisions 'must be decided by Sunday 21:00' and drives acceptance of operational chaos and legal shortcuts
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Explicit framing that without deal 'CS collapses Monday morning triggering CHF 300-500bn deposit insurance claims and global derivatives chaos' - primary justification for accepting all other costs and risks
